paper.citation: Calonico, S., Cattaneo, M. D., and Farrell, M. H. (2018). On the Effect of Bias Estimation on Coverage Accuracy in Nonparametric Inference. Journal of the American Statistical Association 113(522), 767-779. DOI: 10.1080/01621459.2017.1285776.
paper.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
paper.source_locator: Supplement S.II.7 (Complete Simulation Results), printed p.80, PDF p.81: data-generating process Y=m(X)+eps, X~U[-1,1], eps~N(0,1) (homoscedastic), and Model 3 regression function m(x)=0.3*exp(-4*(2x+1)^2)+0.7*exp(-16*(2x-1)^2). Main text Section 4 (Simulation Results), printed p.776, PDF p.10: the five-point evaluation grid x in {-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3,2/3}.

mechanism.name: Nonparametric regression with two Gaussian peaks: CCF2018 Model 3 (homoscedastic)

generation_equations.label: DGP structure
generation_equations.expression: Y = m(X) + eps,  X ~ U[-1,1],  eps ~ N(0,1)  homoscedastic, independently of X

generation_equations.label: Peak locations
generation_equations.expression: left peak at x=-1/2 (amplitude 0.3); right peak at x=1/2 (amplitude 0.7)

assumptions: iid observations; X is independent of the noise eps
eps ~ N(0,1) with mean zero and constant variance (homoscedastic), so E[Y|X=x0] = m(x0) is deterministic and known in closed form
m(x) is smooth (infinitely differentiable); each Gaussian peak is C-infinity; the two peaks are well separated (left at x=-1/2, right at x=1/2)
Pointwise inference at each fixed query point; the five-point grid is NOT evaluated as a simultaneous confidence band by the current scalar truth interface
No causal interpretation; this is a nonparametric regression inference (NRI) task with no treatment, mediator, or intervention

properties.notes: Univariate nonparametric regression (dimension=1, effective_dimension=1: one covariate X fully determines the conditional mean). Nonlinearity from a mixture of two Gaussian peaks: m(x)=0.3*exp(-4*(2x+1)^2)+0.7*exp(-16*(2x-1)^2). Left peak: amplitude 0.3, centered at x=-1/2 (where 2x+1=0), effective width ~1/(2*sqrt(2))~0.35. Right peak: amplitude 0.7, centered at x=1/2 (where 2x-1=0), effective width ~1/(4*sqrt(2))~0.18 (sharper). The two peaks are well separated and create a bimodal regression surface. No interactions, no high-dimensional structure, no irrelevant padding. Note: heteroscedasticity is NOT a property of this scenario (homoscedastic eps~N(0,1)).

estimand.name: m(x0) = E[Y | X = x0]
estimand.definition: Conditional mean of Y given X = x0 at a fixed query point x0 from the grid {-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3,2/3}, in the superpopulation defined by Y = m(X) + eps, X ~ U[-1,1], eps ~ N(0,1) (homoscedastic). Model 3: m(x) = 0.3*exp(-4*(2x+1)^2) + 0.7*exp(-16*(2x-1)^2), a mixture of two Gaussian peaks with the left peak (amplitude 0.3, narrower width) centered at x=-1/2 and the right peak (amplitude 0.7, sharper width) centered at x=1/2. Each query point is a separate pointwise inference target; the five points are not a simultaneous confidence band. This contribution collects only the CCF M3 homoscedastic scenario; the Chen-Qin (2000) two-peak structure m_CQ(x) = m_CCF_M3(2x-1) with heteroscedastic noise, support [0,1], and query points {0,0.5} is a separate contribution because its complete observation law differs.

truth.expression: Conditional mean of Y given X = x0 at a fixed query point x0 from the grid {-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3,2/3}, in the superpopulation defined by Y = m(X) + eps, X ~ U[-1,1], eps ~ N(0,1) (homoscedastic). Model 3: m(x) = 0.3*exp(-4*(2x+1)^2) + 0.7*exp(-16*(2x-1)^2), a mixture of two Gaussian peaks with the left peak (amplitude 0.3, narrower width) centered at x=-1/2 and the right peak (amplitude 0.7, sharper width) centered at x=1/2. Each query point is a separate pointwise inference target; the five points are not a simultaneous confidence band. This contribution collects only the CCF M3 homoscedastic scenario; the Chen-Qin (2000) two-peak structure m_CQ(x) = m_CCF_M3(2x-1) with heteroscedastic noise, support [0,1], and query points {0,0.5} is a separate contribution because its complete observation law differs.
truth.derivation: Direct analytic evaluation of m(x0)=0.3*exp(-4*(2x0+1)^2)+0.7*exp(-16*(2x0-1)^2). Each query point has an exact closed form in terms of exp of rationals: m3(-2/3)=0.3*exp(-4/9)+0.7*exp(-784/9); m3(-1/3)=0.3*exp(-4/9)+0.7*exp(-400/9); m3(0)=0.3*exp(-4)+0.7*exp(-16); m3(1/3)=0.3*exp(-100/9)+0.7*exp(-16/9); m3(2/3)=0.3*exp(-196/9)+0.7*exp(-16/9). Independent verification uses a separately-factored exponent path and peak-pair symmetry identities.
